text:
Digital knowledge bases are great for searchability, but they often become "digital graveyards" for unthought links. When your system feels cluttered and hollow, you don't need a better app—you need a manual fallback.

Writing in a notebook or on physical cards forces you to compress information rather than just copying and pasting. This friction slows down the cognitive process, ensuring you are actually synthesizing ideas instead of just archiving them. If you've lost your way, return to pen and paper to rediscover true clarity.
